newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy court explains re-trial in war crimes case.
newsitem.headline: Italy court explains re-trial in war crimes case.

text.p: The military judge who presided over the war crimes trial of former SS captain Erich Priebke should have removed himself from the case, Italy's highest appeals court said on Thursday in explaining why it ordered a re-trial.
The Court of Cassation ruled on October 15 that Priebke, 83, should be tried again because of irregularities at his trial, which ended in uproar on August 1.

A three-judge panel, headed by Judge Agostino Quistelli, decided in a split verdict that while Priebke was guilty of multiple murder he could not be punished because of mitigating circumstances and expiry of a statute of limitations.
Angry protesters laid siege to the military court, trapping Priebke and the judges inside in a stand-off lasting several hours which only ended when Priebke was re-arrested.
Priebke is accused of helping organise the SS massacre of 335 men and boys in caves outside Rome in March 1944, Italy's worst wartime atrocity.
Priebke admits killing two people, but says he had to follow orders or be killed himself.

In a written decision explaining its October 15 ruling, the Court of Cassation said its re-trial order was based on comments Quistelli made before he was assigned the case last year. In a conversation with a general, Quistelli said he believed Priebke should be cleared on the basis of his defence.

The appeal court said that Quistelli, "like any Italian citizen, is free to express his point of view on whatever argument, even relating to facts of judicial relevance over which he could find himself presiding".
"But that right, once exercised, carries the obligation for a judge entrusted with a trial to stand down," the court said.

Priebke was re-arrested the night of the verdict after Germany indicated it wanted to extradite him for a war crimes trial there. Lawyers say that request would be set aside until after the Italian re-trial, for which no date has yet been set.
Priebke, who had lived openly in Argentina for nearly 50 years, was extradited to Italy in November 1995. He is now being held in a Rome jail.
